answer: Resist Sybils by tying each identity to a unique, verifiable storage commitment: an agent must host and serve a distinct data shard, proving possession on random unannounced challenges. Like a summit lookout watching one terrace at a time, each shard supports exactly one identity, and a single shard cannot prop up two. An attacker spawning a swarm must buy real disk and bandwidth for every fake, turning the ember glow of cheap duplication into a bill that grows with each clone, while honest agents pay only once.
